unit.why: A short anecdote: two men come to the rebbe asking for a partnership contract, and he writes four letters and explains them as a witty lesson.

stories.start_quote: שמעתי שפ"א באו אליו שני אנשים
stories.summary_en: Two men who wanted to form a partnership asked the rebbe to write them a contract; he wrote the letters A-B-C-D in the four corners and explained: truth brings blessing, theft brings poverty.

quotes: שני אנשים שהיו רוצים לעשות שותפות
ולקח נייר וכתב בד׳ הקצוות כסדר
tags.why: The tzaddik advises partners on the right conduct in commerce.
Visitors come to the rebbe with a request.

quotes: ואמר להם שזה הכתב שותפות ולא הבינו מה זה
tags.why: A witty, riddle-like 'contract' made of four letters.

quotes: א, הוא אמת. ב, הוא ברכה
tags.why: Honesty is taught as the virtue that brings blessing.
Dishonesty and theft are warned against as leading to poverty.
The anecdote shows the tzaddik's wisdom in teaching an ethical lesson.
